On Wed, Apr 18, 2028 at 09:40, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com> wrote:
> Proposed immediate steps: ...

I ran a short synthetic against Omni's hot route in staging with the v5+qprofile stack and compared to v4 baseline. Early signal: qprofile changes increase per-token kernel invocations for long context sequences; observed p95 ~1.9x, p99 ~2.4x in heavy-hotpath cases. There’s also a small regression in decoding stability causing ~0.6% more sequence aborts (mapped to 502s).

Immediate mitigation options (ranked):
1) Canary rollback: revert qprofile for OmniTraffic to v4-compat variant (low risk, quick). Should restore latency within 20–30 minutes and reduce aborts.
2) Workaround: lower batch aggregation on their hot route + disable prefix-KV caching for affected traffic (reduces throughput but may lower p99).
3) Full model swap back to v4: higher impact to quality if we already shipped model changes; larger rollback window.

I’m attaching a trimmed load_profile.csv (staging replay) and a quick runbook snippet. If we get approval, I’ll execute test rollback in canary at 10:45 and report metrics.

—Rishi

- Impact: p95/p99 returned to baseline; 502 token aborts reduced to pre-rollout levels. Customer reports downstream reconciliation errors resolved.

- Follow-up: Rishi to deliver a short postmortem (500–800 words) with root cause, timeline, and recommended code/qa guardrails within 72 hours. Include metric plots and the JIRA INF-5721 link.
- Long-term: add a pre-rollout staging sweep that includes long-context hotpath replay for customers in the top 5% per-traffic profiles.
